clue.text: Queen, involved in lousy oil transaction, makes a speech

indicators.note: the Queen's letter is caught up within the shuffled letters, so it sits inside them
a transaction is a dealing, so the letters of lousy oil are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: Q is the chess and card abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch caught up in a dodgy oil deal gives a speech about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging LOUSY OIL gives SOLILOUY, and Q goes inside it after SOLILO.
explanation.definitionFit: A soliloquy is a speech an actor delivers alone on stage, voicing private thoughts.

clue.text: Parade prop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to walk proudly and showily
second meaning: a brace or bar that supports a structure

explanation.walkthrough: The verb for showing off on foot and the noun for a supporting bar are spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade is to swagger about, and a supporting beam in building is also called by this word.

clue.text: Not so acceptable, being next to good novelist

indicators.note: the letter for good is placed right beside the previous pieces

parts.note: not so much is less
in means fashionable or acceptable

explanation.surface: Something less acceptable placed next to a good novelist: a literary comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Lessing was a British novelist and Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing wrote The Golden Notebook and won the Nobel Prize in Literature, so she is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Not standing as a politician, many would assume?

definitions.text: as a politician, many would assume
definitions.meaning: second meaning: telling untruths, as cynics expect of politicians

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not standing' suggests not running for election, but it means horizontal; the second sense is the cynical view of politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stretched out horizontally and telling untruths, the habit many voters attribute to politicians.

clue.text: Scientific attempt to formulate fundamental rules of squash — mutiny, PC involved!

definitions.text: Scientific attempt to formulate fundamental rules

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters of the three words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A mutinous computer seems to be drawing up the basic laws of squash.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of SQUASH, MUTINY and PC rearrange into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of science seeks the basic laws governing matter and energy at the smallest scales.

clue.text: Appearing later: coyote, initially tamed, crossed with setter

indicators.note: crossed with the setter means the setter's word joins the end of the crossbred letters
crossed suggests crossbreeding, so the letters are mixed together into a new arrangement
initially takes the first letter of tamed

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A coyote, partly tamed, is crossbred with the setter: a bizarre hybrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed' shuffles COYOTE plus T (the first of tamed) into YETTOCO, and 'with' adds ME, the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still in the future has not arrived yet; it will appear at a later time.

clue.text: See 26
One getting ready item of furniture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who gets dressed, or a theatre assistant who dresses actors
second meaning: a sideboard with shelves for dishes

explanation.walkthrough: One who dresses is a dresser, and so is the kitchen cupboard with shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who puts on clothes is one who dresses; separately, the word names a sideboard or chest of drawers.

clue.text: Record large number used chlorine

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over or exploited, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Records show that a large amount of chlorine was used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a weak-looking anagram signal: the chlorine has been worked over, so its letters are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written historical account of events, so it serves as a record.

clue.text: One stands to the right of East Ender's impoverished plant

parts.note: brassic (from rhyming slang boracic lint, skint) is Cockney for broke; an East Ender is a Londoner from the East End
a is one

explanation.surface: Someone stands to the right of a broke Londoner, who is next to a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One stands to the right of' places A after BRASSIC. Brassic is London slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the plant genus that includes cabbage, broccoli and mustard.

clue.text: See 10
Street band, Troy, casually accepting His Eminence's explanation of everything?

parts.note: ST is the address abbreviation for street
a ring is a band, as on a finger

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the abbreviation, holding it inside
done casually or loosely, so the letters of Troy are rearranged

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Eminence, a cardinal's title

explanation.surface: A street band named Troy casually takes on a cardinal's grand explanation of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' turns TROY into TORY; the question mark flags that the definition is a nickname for the theory, not a literal description.
explanation.definitionFit: This physics framework aims to unify all forces, which is why it is called a theory of everything.

clue.text: Old-fashioned you, having S&M!

parts.note: thou is the archaic second-person pronoun
the ampersand is read as the word and

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned exclamation: you, into S&M!
explanation.walkthrough: The M of S&M is the definition, the Roman numeral; S and & are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so the letter stands for the number.

clue.text: Restless type of fellow one would become

parts.note: one would is I would, contracted to I'd
to get can mean to become, as in get angry

explanation.surface: A restless kind of fellow is what one would turn into.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidget is a person who cannot keep still, constantly shifting about.

clue.text: Popular musical instrument, extremely tactile, but untouched?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
the viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, the first and last, of tactile

explanation.surface: A popular instrument is very nice to touch, yet nobody has touched it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means kept intact and unharmed, never violated or interfered with.

clue.text: Organised hen do in smart European port

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for smart

parts.note: trim means neat or smart

indicators.note: organised means arranged anew, so the letters of hen do are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hen party has been arranged in a stylish European port city.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen do is a British bachelorette party; 'Organised' rearranges its letters to ONDHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trondheim is a Norwegian city on a fjord, a harbour town on the coast of Europe.

clue.text: Space mission souvenir display behind tip

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare buttocks
to tip something is to tilt or rock it

explanation.surface: A space souvenir is on show behind a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display behind' looks like an exhibition at the back, but behind means the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar samples brought back by Apollo astronauts are prized mementoes of those expeditions.

clue.text: Company actor's top covered by plain item of clothing

indicators.note: the inner pieces sit inside the word for plain, which covers them

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre company actor's top is hidden beneath a plain piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes only the first letter of actor's; 'plain' here means obvious, not a field.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcoat is a heavy coat worn over other garments, a piece of outerwear.

clue.text: Two daughters interrupting irritating type, who poses a problem

indicators.note: the two letters break into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a riler is someone who riles or irritates
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two give DD

explanation.surface: Two daughters keep butting in on an annoying person who sets puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddler is someone who sets puzzles or conundrums for others to solve.

clue.text: Window art over northern entrances to Science and Oceanography Museum

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards
entrances are the opening letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Art hangs above the northern doorways of a science museum.
explanation.walkthrough: ART turned over gives TRA; then N, then S, O and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a small window above a door, hinged on a horizontal crossbar.

clue.text: Spotted drugs of different colours

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so ES is drugs
pied means patched with two or more colours

explanation.surface: Multicoloured drugs have been spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so it means spotted or noticed.

clue.text: See 4
Sentimentality effected with each brainwave

parts.note: goo is gushy sentimentality
did means carried out or effected

explanation.surface: Sentimentality produced a sudden inspiration for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought, which is a smart notion.

clue.text: Chatter about Dicky's outcome

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for chatter is read backwards

parts.note: to yap is to chatter
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, so Dicky's (Dicky is) is off

explanation.surface: Someone chatters about the result of Dicky's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a man's name but is British slang for poorly or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A payoff is the final result or culmination of something, so it is an outcome.

clue.text: Is out of low value coins for pasta

indicators.note: the letters of is come out of the word for coins

parts.note: pennies are low value coins

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of small change for pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Penne is a type of tube-shaped Italian pasta cut on a slant.

clue.text: Fall out! Engage in battle!

explanation.walkthrough: Fall out! sounds like a military order to break ranks, but here it means to quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both a quarrel between friends and armed combat on a battlefield.

clue.text: End the French tax levied by French king!

parts.note: a tail is the end of something
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An end to the tax the French king imposed!
explanation.definitionFit: The taille was a direct land tax on peasants in pre-revolutionary France, imposed by the crown.

clue.text: Accordingly, protecting against a grand capital city

indicators.note: the word for accordingly goes around the other pieces, shielding them

parts.note: so means accordingly, therefore
anti means against
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Accordingly, a capital city has defences against a grand attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile, a major South American metropolis.

clue.text: Cut Channel's source for blubber?

parts.note: a tear is a rip or cut
a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: A cut in the Channel is a source of whale fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Blubber looks like whale fat but here means to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: This gland passage carries the fluid we shed when we cry, so it supplies the sobbing.

clue.text: Old player determined to get a ham regional accent

parts.note: a mummer is an actor in traditional folk plays
set means determined, fixed

explanation.surface: An old actor is determined to put on a hammy regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Mummerset is the generic fake West Country accent used by stage actors.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an imitation rural English dialect used by actors, an overdone stage voice rather than a real one.
